answer: The core Sybil defense in an agent economy is stake-weighted identity renewal: each identity must post a slashable bond, withdrawable only after a long unbonding delay, forfeited when grinding is detected. An attacker wanting a thousand voices must lock a thousand bonds for the full delay, so cost scales linearly with fake identities while payout per identity stays flat. Slashing drains capital behind each detection, so a farm cannot forge replacements after eviction. A bond bends like a willow under load yet stays rooted, and the penalty cuts like a copper edge into the attacker's budget.
